title: A Burg of Quips
subtitle: Indeed, he's never missed an opportunity for a quip.

items.text: A Burg of Quips
Roland wrings out the water that is pooling on the hem of his clothes.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Rain again …

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Hmph … Where is everyone?
The trail left by their attacker had disappeared.
And his fellow knights had disappeared along with it.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Hm?
Hoof beats tramp across the mud nearby.
He holds his breath and listens.
The figure of a knight appears in the distance, causing Roland to draw his sword defensively.
… Roland?

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Oliver! You nearly drove me out of my wits!

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Haha …
Roland mounts his horse, and the pair ride side by side in the rain.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: So—

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Was it really Ganelon who suggested a festival of jokes? He doesn't seem the type to enjoy comedy.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Then no sooner than our comrade had called himself "Roland," he was struck dead in the attack …

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: It is as I said, there is great power in a joke.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: They can inspire morale while marching or on the eve of battle.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: I can remember many a time when a well-timed joke has done much to lift the spirits of a weary band.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: If I may speak out of turn, my friend. I feel I must tell you something.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Roland, bosom friend, I think perhaps your jokes serve only one purpose.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: To inspire a timely retreat.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: I regret only that my love for comedy as yet outstretches my talent.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: You should know, I suspect a traitor among our fellowship. If they plan to strike again, their next move will be in Paimpont Forest.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: They will not make the same mistake twice—we must move with haste.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Regardless, I'm heartened to see you are safe—may our Lord continue to protect you, Roland.
He reaches out to pat his friend's shoulder.
But in a flash, Roland draws his sword and swings in a fierce motion towards Oliver's ear.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: D**n it!
The blade catches the arrow mid-flight, cutting it in twain.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Ride for the forest. We'll talk about the rest later.
Hearkening to his liege's orders, Oliver bends down, grasping the horse's belly with his legs, and spurs it into a gallop towards the forest.
But a second arrow reaches them first, piercing the destrier's leg and spilling both horse and rider on the ground.
Oliver falls hard on his leg and lays stunned on the ground.

items.speaker: Attacker I
items.text: It's Oliver!
The attacker grins and raises the sword in his hand.

items.speaker: Attacker I
items.text: His head won't be as valuable as Roland, still …
The lumbering figure's shadow engulfs Oliver's body.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Careful—
Roland rides swiftly, holding high his Everlasting Sword. With a single stroke, he cleaves the shadow in two.
A short, stiff cry gives way to the sudden wash of warm liquid that spills out over Oliver.

items.speaker: Attacker II
items.text: D**n it …

items.speaker: Attacker II
items.text: Why are you retreating?! There are but two of them!

items.speaker: Attacker II
items.text: Ulch—
There is a sudden coldness in the attacker's throat.
His vision begins to spin, a dizzying sensation as he falls to the ground.
From the ground, he sees his own headless corpse slouching off the back of his horse.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Quick, Oliver, take my hand—
The salt from the blood is stinging his eyes. Oliver forces them to open.
In the blurred vision, he catches sight of Roland's figure and reaches out his hand toward him.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: They'll be expecting us to move forward, further into their ambush. Don't follow the path they're driving us towards … Go around!
Roland grasps his comrade and hoists him up onto his horse.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Not to worry, young Oliver. I'm no fresh squire.
The horse carries the two knights deep into the forest.
The rain grows heavier, and its rhythmic tapping gradually swallows up all other sounds.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Ah, this little cave here will serve as an able refuge through the rain.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: A cave? Perhaps you should check inside for wild beasts first …
The pain still keeps him from seeing straight.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: No need to fret. We'll be safe in here. Come now. Let's see about your shoulder and leg.
They stash themselves in the hollow cave, lying down on a bed of damp green moss.
Roland draws his long sword and severs the shaft of an errant arrow still clinging harmlessly to his armor.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Did you hear those hooves, not far in the distance?

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Almost twenty men were chasing us—every one of them equipped with armor, swords, and a cordon of arrows.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: But we're still alive, Oliver.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: … So? There is danger here, Roland—it's not just about our immediate crisis.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Someone wants you to die here.
An eerie silence falls over the forest, as if the rain has hushed itself.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Oliver, look.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: There's an Arachne.
Oliver's neck goes rigid.
It is a venomous spider critter, one that prefers to nest in damp, dark places.
He looks slowly in the direction of Roland's gaze—
Roland has folded his hands together, shaping them like a spider, crawling through the air.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Ro-land!
Oliver cannot stand it anymore. He slams his fist down hard on the ground.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: How many times do we have to tell you—these jokes of ours are not funny!

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Our foes number twenty at least, likely more with reinforcements … And there are only the two of us!

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Tell me how you manage to conjure these horrid jokes in a situation like this?!

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: I thought you needed something to raise your mood.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: It's only managed to raise my ire!

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Roland, my liege ... allow me to suggest what we should do now …
A plan is forming in his mind, one that seems to ease his pain.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: They know that you were to reach Brittany today.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: But they didn't know that I would ride here to receive you.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: If the worst should come to pass, you may be able to escape by wearing my cloak …
There is a second flash of genius on his face.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Yes—

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: This could well be our best opportunity to expose the traitor …
Though the traitor's identity is not difficult for them to guess. He has known the answer for a while.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: It is a sound plan, young Oliver. But I refuse it. If I should do as you say, then only one of us can leave.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: A plan that lets one of us escape is better than both of us dying here.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Don't tell me you're going out there by yourself.
A familiar trumpet sounds far in the distance.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Enemies!

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Friends!
They shout in a clashing unison.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Did that arrow hit your ear after all? That was clear as day the sound of Lady Oder's trumpet call!

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: A trumpet is just an instrument. Anyone can blow it.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Besides, what if Oder has been captured? What if the attackers and Oder simply have the same sort of trumpet?

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Forget it then. There's no use arguing about something you can hear with your own ears. Besides, if not Oder, who else would blow a trumpet like that?

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: She's your sister, and still you cannot recognize her?

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: That may be her, yes, but is it not prudent to consider the other possibilities?

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Indeed, I dare not question His Majesty's decree, but seeing you, our Lord Margrave, reduced to hiding in a cave, I must admit my fear for the future of Brittany.
The Margrave?
It dawns on him.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: You have the right of it.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Great, then we do as I suggested …

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Knight Oliver, I order you to stay here.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Once the danger is gone and you are able, you are to travel to Brittany and relay what has happened here.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Should events transpire that lead to my death, I will recommend that you succeed me as the Margrave of Brittany.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Don't worry. I'll pen a letter to His Majesty, listing a few of the reasons for "making Sir Oliver your trusted Margrave." I'll use all the most colorful rhetoric at my disposal.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: I think you've confused our situation for a fairy tale, my Lord Margrave.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Suppose you die out there, Roland, on whatever fool heroic you're planning, and I survive to present your letter of recommendation to His Majesty's Court ...

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: What do you earnestly think they would do if I were to show up in your place?

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: I'm very sure, after reading through my glowing recommendation, they would grant you the title of Margrave of Brittany.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: I see now why His Majesty so appreciates your honest nature, Sir Roland.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: But think seriously, surely they would start to wonder why I decided to ride out to meet you.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: And the why-fores and whens of how you died, and how it came to be that there was no one else around to witness your death.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: If I were then to present a letter of your recommendation, how would it be received?

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: You are suggesting they would think you forged the letter. Perhaps even that you orchestrated this ambush.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: You think too poorly of His Majesty's Court. The Paladins of Charlemagne are good and just.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Roland, you can't just split people into simple categories of "good" and "evil."

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: People are complicated, and men of power more complicated still—you should know that far better than I do.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: Besides …
He falls silent again.
The weight of the accusation bore on him, to accuse one of their brethren of treachery, he hesitates to continue.
Roland pats his shoulder.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Go on.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: The traitor must be one of the other Paladins, one of your brothers in Charlemagne's court.
A sharp stab of pain throbs in his shoulder. Oliver takes a deep breath before continuing.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: It is Ganelon of Mainz.
Roland breaks into a grin.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: That's reassuring, Oliver.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: You finally learned how to make a joke.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: Oh … Don't misunderstand. There is weight to your speculation.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: But, it's a matter of proof …
The trumpet sounds out once again, now much closer than before.
Before long, a party of knights emerges from the surrounding forest, led by a woman.

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: Oh—Sir Roland, how did you end up here?

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: Don't worry, old friend. My men made short work of your would-be assassins—we even managed to seize them alive, the lion's share at any rate.

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: The both of you look worse for wear; we must make for the castle quickly.

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: But first … A question!

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: What did the blanket say to the bed?
Roland answers without missing a beat.

items.speaker: Roland
items.text: I've got you covered.

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: Aha! Precisely! I've got you covered!
Brittany Fortress
The rain washes down the narrow streets of the castle town.
The smells of blood from the butcher shop, of ammonia from the tannery, and the reek of old sweat that had long lingered there are swept out by the arrival of the rain.
But no pleasant scent of earth and stone greets her. The reek of fish clings on in wet weather, as bits of fish covered in scales float on the puddles over Oder's feet.

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: We need someone charismatic to lead the interrogation. May I propose the Knight of Astorford?

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: Should he fail to win them over with charm, then we must rely on Lord Reynaud to break them.

items.speaker: Oder
items.text: But to have these two noblemen come to interrogate such a prisoner …

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: There's no need to involve them, my lady. We have our own manner of guile to make the brigand talk.

items.speaker: Oliver
items.text: For now, let us take Roland to rest. I believe the journey has finally caught up to him.
Roland, at last exhausted from his journey and battle, begins to slump in his saddle. The voices around him grow fainter.
Until all sound blends into the patter of the rain.
He closes his eyes, and darkness swallows everything like a tide.
*thud, thud, thud*

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Oof!
A Knight's Room

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: Whoa …!
The two of them barge through the door and tumble into the sunlit room.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh! You have some visitors.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: Ah, Sir Knight, so you've been in your room this whole time!

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: Hmph, then all that fuss about the lights was just old circuits. Ms. Vertin should hire an electrician!

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: There's no need for concern. Someone is here, as they have been for some time.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: APPLe can attest to this. We preferred to use just the sunlight in this room, as it created a very dramatic lighting effect for Mr. Knight.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: We're holding a bit of a storytelling session.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Quite so. Someone was just in the middle of a story about Sir Roland ... However, Sir APPLe here seems to believe that one's storytelling skills are lacking—

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone has been attempting to portray the figure of a knight named Roland in order to immerse the audience in the moment.
The knight's gauntlets spread and lower on both sides, approximating a theatrical bow.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone is pleased that you happened by.
TO BE CONTINUED…
